quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Deutsche Bank’s Chicago Industrials Summit 2026 (08-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak (the first month as the new pure-play automation company): orders in July 'are looking good', which is why Honeywell raised its guidance. The three-year targets are 4%-6% top-line growth, doubled EPS growth to reach $12 in 2029, strong margin expansion and 90% plus free capital conversion, with 'points of contingency' built in for demand disruption, inflation or pricing not being at 4%. In the second half 'we'll grow 4%-6%... Hopefully, more closer to 6%', a good setup for 2027, especially the first half; for 2027 EPS growth 'I'm looking at like a 15%'. Margin expansion is more pronounced this year and next (stranded costs coming off), returning to the more normal 60 basis points a year in 2028 and 2029. Regions: Europe is no longer a headwind, China is 'doing okay', the Middle East is 'surprisingly' strong and North America is 'real strong'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2H growth 4%-6% (hopefully closer to 6%); 2027 EPS growth like a 15%; $12 EPS in 2029; 60 basis points annual margin expansion in 2028-2029

quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Deutsche Bank’s Chicago Industrials Summit 2026 (08-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak on Building Automation: the business has 'a good runway to be able to grow at mid-single digits plus'; Honeywell is not guiding high single digits to leave the team room to experiment and to manage for the longer term. Building Automation will finish this year 'north of 27%' segment margin with 'a really good line of sight' to a 29% margin in 2029, driven by new product introductions, Honeywell Forge and employee leverage; Forge is most penetrated in Building Automation, then Process Automation. New product introductions generally become accretive within the first two years and come with better price or mix, and Honeywell gets its best outcomes when it consistently allocates 4%-4.5% of revenue to R&D.
quarterly_data.figure: Building Automation margin north of 27% in 2026, 29% in 2029; R&D 4%-4.5% of revenue

quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Deutsche Bank’s Chicago Industrials Summit 2026 (08-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak on data centers: data centers are about 5% of Building Automation (close to zero about three, four years ago) and growing 'tremendously'; 'We would like our data center business to double over the next few years. So we would like to be over $1 billion. And it should be 10% of the building automation business', with Building Automation eventually a $10 billion business. Today's data-center sales are mainly fire sensing, physical security and monitoring and building management systems; as new data centers require their own power source Honeywell sees opportunity in managing and sensing the load and its stability, and 'We have a lot of great technology that we are launching on sensing, liquid cooling, measuring heat'.
quarterly_data.figure: data centers about 5% of Building Automation; target over $1 billion and 10% of Building Automation; Building Automation $10 billion eventually

quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Deutsche Bank’s Chicago Industrials Summit 2026 (08-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak on LNG: 'For our LNG business, we are taking orders now for slots in the end of 2028. We are building out capacity in our LNG business to continue to support the demand', with new customers coming in 'essentially almost daily'; the LNG capacity spend is contained within overall capex of around 3% of revenue (a more capex-light company after the Solstice and Honeywell Aerospace separations). Middle East rebuild orders will show partly in 2027 revenue - the drawings exist and getting the product through manufacturing is the constraint.
quarterly_data.figure: LNG orders for slots at the end of 2028; capex around 3% of revenue

quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Deutsche Bank’s Chicago Industrials Summit 2026 (08-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak on Process Automation and Technology: catalyst demand is inflecting as customers reload facilities with oil prices staying higher for longer - up double digits in the second half versus the first half, about flat for the year and up high single digits year over year in the second half - but projects (backlog conversion) drive the segment's second-half growth; outside the Middle East new-facility build-out is broad in Africa, Asia and Latin America. Process technologies orders are picking up more than process automation, which runs about 18 to 24 months behind, is 'kind of flattish' and will grow faster next year while moving into life sciences, pharma, medical devices, cyber, U.S. onshoring and semiconductors. SVP Investor Relations Mark Macaluso: a couple of multi-hundred million dollar orders in Q3 and Q4 of last year make tough comparisons; CFO: process technology orders could be down in the fourth quarter, maybe the third, but book-to-bill is 'way above one'. Segment margin will be about 22.5% for the year, about 150 basis points lower year over year on mix and the dilutive Johnson Matthey integration; confidence in the 25% 2029 target is 'high', with Johnson Matthey reaching Honeywell margins taking 2, 3 years.
quarterly_data.figure: PA&T margin about 22.5% in 2026 (about 150 basis points lower); 25% target for 2029; process automation 18 to 24 months behind process technologies

quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Deutsche Bank’s Chicago Industrials Summit 2026 (08-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak on Industrial Automation (now a pure-play sensing and measurement business): on time to first promise is about 80%, targeted north of 85%, with on time to Customer One Day the more important metric; growth of single digits plus in the second half and 'a really good line of sight' to double digits next year from new products and execution; about a 22% margin rate in the fourth quarter and '100% confident' in the 25% three-year margin target. Industrial Automation is close to a $4 billion business that Honeywell would like to be $7 billion, 'much harder to get to $7 billion without doing any M&A'; bolt-on M&A of a $2 billion-$4 billion ticket size is focused mainly on Industrial Automation, must be accretive, in the sensing and measurement core and reach a 10% ROI by year 5; a large transformational deal is 'probably not a priority'.
quarterly_data.figure: on time to first promise about 80% (target north of 85%); about 22% Q4 margin; 25% margin target; close to $4 billion business, $7 billion ambition; $2 billion-$4 billion bolt-on M&A

quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Deutsche Bank’s Chicago Industrials Summit 2026 (08-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak on software: growth in software and services is 'really Forge' - Honeywell connected more assets last year than in the five years prior, has about 5 million connected assets today and will connect about 9 million in total over the next two and a half years, which underpins the 15% annual software revenue growth; Honeywell builds AI models from the connected assets for customers, and customer response has been 'Very good'. Internally Honeywell made 'a big investment' equipping all associates with AI tools and Copilots, used in engineering for drafting, drawings, retrievals and proposals ('tens of thousands of hours of productivity') and in finance and internal audit.
quarterly_data.figure: about 5 million connected assets, about 9 million in total over the next two and a half years; 15% annual software revenue growth
